newsitem.title: CHINA: Chinese yuan ends up at seven-week high vs dollar.
newsitem.headline: Chinese yuan ends up at seven-week high vs dollar.

text.p: The Chinese yuan ended slightly up at a seven-week high close of 8.2949 from Thursday's 8.2951 against the U.S. dollar in Shanghai due to China's surging foreign trade surplus, traders said.
It was the highest close since February 26 when the yuan finaished at 8.2946.
The weighted average price on Thursday was 8.2951.

Dealers said pro-yuan sentiment remained strong on the market after the announcement on Monday of a foreign trade surplus of $6.71 billion in the first three months of this year, up 25.7 percent from the same period last year.

The yuan opened down at an intraday low of 8.2955 and rose slightly to move in a narrow range of 8.2950 and 8.2952 for most of the session before it edging up again, hitting a high of 8.2948 right before the close.
Trading was dull with most business done at 8.2951.
One dealer said it was first time in the past seven weeks that the yuan had closed above the 8.2950 resistance level.
"The trade surplus was the key factor pushing the yuan up this week," he said. "Buying for the yuan has emerged due to expectations that more dollars will flow into the market."
A second dealer said the yuan was unlikely to hold above the 8.2950 level early next week despite Friday's rise.
"The yuan traded mostly below 8.2950 today, suggesting it won't be able to stand firm above that level early next week," he said.
Dealers said they expected the yuan to move around 8.2950 next Monday.
The yuan closed down at an intraday low of 6.6380 from 6.5991 against 100 Japanese yen and up at 1.0700 from 1.0715 against the Hong Kong dollar.
